claims.statement: For finite disjoint positive-size blocks with B_i=(1+z)^{r_i}+z, the exact weighted-subset identity and singleton-event Jensen lower bound hold for 0<=k<=M; the zero-extended coefficient floor may be convolved with the nonnegative path-star marked factor GF_{r_i}.
claims.scope: The registered special-factor occupancy/Jensen claim only: positive block sizes, empty block family allowed, in-range probability formulas, zero-extended coefficient floor, and nonnegative path-star convolution. It does not assert parent-rank transfer, strict selectors, marked-deletion identities in other graphs, MASS, payment, or arbitrary-tree compensation.
claims.reason: The special B_r statement follows from the exact finite-block proof recorded here; the boundary checks agree. No independence assumption is used for the dependent block-count vector.

claims.statement: For a finite family of positive block sizes r_i with M=sum_i r_i, and real polynomials F_i=sum_{t=0}^{r_i} f_i(t)z^t with f_i(t)>=choose(r_i,t), define H=product_i F_i and y_k=sum_i sum_{t=0}^{r_i} choose(r_i,t)choose(M-r_i,k-t)/choose(M,k) * 2(f_i(t)-choose(r_i,t))/(f_i(t)+choose(r_i,t)). For every 0<=k<=M and natural d, H[k]>=choose(M,k) E_d(y_k), where E_d(y)=sum_{a=0}^d y^a/a!. Include empty family M=k=0, with H[0]=1 and y_0=0.
claims.scope: Universal abstract finite-block coefficient/Jensen theorem, with positive integer block sizes and nonnegative coefficient surplus, plus empty family. Probability normalization is only used in 0<=k<=M; all binomial coefficients outside range are zero-extended. No graph rank, marked deletion, strict selector, MASS, payment, or arbitrary-tree conclusion.
claims.reason: Count-vector enumeration gives the normalized coefficient as E product_i w_i(K_i); Jensen and log(w)>=2(w-1)/(w+1) give exp(y_k). Since y_k>=0, the finite Taylor sum E_d(y_k) is a lower bound. Exact rational checks cover 17 boundary/interior cases; no Lean award is claimed.

claims.statement: For each finite graph factor H_i of independence number r_i, I(H_i)[t]>=choose(r_i,t); if H_i has a vertex outside a fixed maximum independent set, then I(H_i)[t]>=(1+z)^{r_i}+z coefficientwise. Applying the finite-block bound to a product of such factors is valid when the required disjoint-component factorization is separately established.
claims.scope: Coefficient domination and fixed-rank product lower bounds only. Any payment application additionally needs exact parent/deletion factorization and the original-tag multiplicities at every same eligible p.
claims.reason: Subsets of a maximum independent set establish the binomial coefficients, and an outside singleton supplies the degree-one surplus. Those coefficient facts alone carry none of the parent-rank or marked-deletion structure.
